label: accepted

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read instantly as a cross-hilt longsword (pointed blade, upturned guard tips, ringed grip, disc pommel); top view is only a thin guard bar as expected for any sword, and the outline is mirror-even with A15 X/Y = 0.0.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: long blade dominates, guard and disc pommel as medium masses, gem, fuller and grip rings as small detail; no uniform noise.
evidence.V3: Safe, near-realistic proportions rather than confident stylisation: the blade is a long, near-constant-width prism with a short tip taper, the grip is thin next to the chunky guard, and the flat disc pommel is small and reads weakly at distance; the upturned guard tips are the only real exaggeration.
evidence.V4: Consistent ~kit-size chamfers catch light on the guard top edges and lobe, pommel disc rim and collar, and blade edge bevels/fuller in the guard and blade-mid close-ups; nothing razor-sharp or blobby.
evidence.V5: Guard, blade-mid, tip and pommel close-ups are clean with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or patches; gate A17/A18 pass with 0 self-intersections, 0 cap overlaps, 0 flipped faces (172 cross-shell overlaps are intentional inserts such as blade into guard). The pommel disc rim shows a faintly polygonal outline only at extreme close range, not a shading artifact.
evidence.V6: Disciplined kit palette: gold guard/pommel, two steel greys plus dark fuller, one accent hue (teal) in two values on grip and gem; crimson and shadow colourways swap only the accent hue cleanly.
evidence.V7: 2424 tris vs weapon target 2500 (ceiling 4000): at/under target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, kit gold/steel/accent palette and matching chamfer scale and smooth shading; sits naturally alongside the kit swords.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Tool Handle, origin at hand/grip point, Hull collision, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic.

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read instantly as a cross-hilted longsword (pointed tip, upturned guard, ringed grip, disc pommel); top view is the expected thin guard bar with blade section; A15 X/Y error 0.0, no lopsided outline.

evidence.V6: Disciplined: gold accent, two steel greys, one teal hue in wrap and gem; colourways swap only the accent hue (crimson, shadow) cleanly with good value contrast.
evidence.V7: 2424 tris vs weapon target 2500 (ceiling 4000), at target.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, kit gold/steel/teal palette, ~kit chamfer width and smooth shading; guard and grip language match the kit sword family.

evidence.V1: Front and silhouette read instantly as a sword (long tapered blade, upturned cross-guard, disc pommel); outline is mirror-clean, A15 X/Y error 0.0; top view is only the guard strip, as expected for a blade.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: long fullered blade (big), gold cross-guard with gem bulge (medium), banded grip, collar and faceted gem (small).
evidence.V3: Blade is confidently long and slim with a good ogive tip, but the guard is a near-uniform flat slab with only a slight end upturn, the grip is short for a longsword (one-hand length), and the thin flat disc pommel undersells the bottom end - partly stylised, partly stiff.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers: blade edge and fuller bevels catch light along the full length, guard edges and tips show even bevel highlights, pommel rim bevelled.
evidence.V5: Pommel disc shows stray low-segment faceting in the studio close-up (visible flat facets on the rim band and dome, polygonal outline in flat light); blade, tip and guard otherwise clean with no seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: steel greys (2 values, dark fuller), gold accent with darker band, one teal hue on grip and gem; colourways swap only the single hue.
evidence.V7: 2424 tris vs weapon target 2500 (ceiling 4000) - at target.
evidence.V8: Kit palette (gold, steel greys, teal), one white vertex-colour material, chamfer scale and smooth shading match the kit anchors closely.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Tool Handle, origin at grip point, Hull collision, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic.

artifacts: Pommel disc rim shows visible polygon segments on its outline in the pommel close-up (minor, silhouette faceting rather than shading)
Gem is low-poly faceted (reads as intentional cut)
Pommel disc: visible faceting on rim and dome from low radial segment count (close_pommel_studio / close_pommel_flat)
Gem is a low-poly faceted cap (reads as intentional cut, minor)
top_fixes: Push stylised proportion: give the blade a stronger taper or a wider ricasso-to-tip flare and a bolder tip so it is not a uniform prism
Thicken the grip slightly and enlarge/heighten the pommel (taller disc or faceted cap) so the hilt end reads at 64 px
Differentiate the guard from the stock flat-bar-with-lobe hilt (deeper upsweep, quillon end caps or stepped profile) to give the longsword its own identity
Raise the pommel disc segment count a little to remove the faint polygonal rim in close-ups (budget headroom is small, so take tris from the grip rings if needed)
Rework the pommel: a larger ball, lobed or wheel pommel instead of the squat flat disc so the bottom reads as a weapon end, not a stand base, and raise its rim segment count
Push stylised proportion: widen the guard span and exaggerate its upturn, or add a slight blade taper/flare near the ricasso so the long blade is not a plain straight run
Differentiate the guard from the existing paddle-crossguard-with-gem sword in the kit (e.g. quillon terminals or a distinct boss shape) so the longsword has its own identity
Raise radial segments (or add support loops/smooth normals) on the pommel disc and collar to remove visible faceting
Give the guard more shape: taper thickness toward the tips and push the upturn/flare so it is not a flat slab (currently near-identical to the Broadsword guard)
Lengthen the grip toward a hand-and-a-half proportion and replace the thin disc pommel with a chunkier wheel or faceted pommel to balance the long blade
